avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a terrace.name: Burgundy by the glass on a tourist terrace
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a terrace.teaser: The Place Carnot terraces pour anonymous regional Bourgogne at a monument-side markup
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a terrace.story: The big café terraces on Place Carnot sell a glass of plain regional Bourgogne at a price set by the view, and the label rarely tells you who made it or which slope it came from. In a town where the wine changes every few hundred metres of hillside, that glass explains nothing. The wine that does is poured in a cellar or at a counter by someone who chose the bottle and can name the grower, the village and the vintage. Sit on the terrace for an espresso and the Saturday crowd; take the wine somewhere else.
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a terrace.why: Keep the square for coffee and people-watching, and spend the wine money where the bottle has a name.
facts: Order a coffee on Place Carnot, then walk ten minutes to a counter where the grower is on the label
Enstase or Caves Madeleine for a glass with a person behind it; the Marché aux Vins for a tasting through the cellars

avoid:The frozen-snail menu.name: The frozen-snail menu
avoid:The frozen-snail menu.teaser: 'Escargots de Bourgogne' near the Hôtel-Dieu are rarely Burgundian: ask where the snails come from
avoid:The frozen-snail menu.story: Around the monuments, set menus open with a dozen 'escargots de Bourgogne' in garlic-and-parsley butter, usually frozen and ready-made. The name is the species, Helix pomatia, not the origin. France has controlled the picking of wild Burgundy snails since a ministerial decree of 24 April 1979, issued because the snail had grown scarce: none may be taken under 3 cm, none at all from 1 April to 30 June, and each département can ban picking outright. Most of what reaches the plate is imported. An honest kitchen will tell you which you are getting.
avoid:The frozen-snail menu.why: Ask the waiter where the snails were picked or farmed; the answer tells you about the whole kitchen.
facts: Ask, before ordering, whether the snails are Helix pomatia and where they come from
Ma Cuisine, whose menu carries escargots à la bourguignonne (dinner only, closed Sunday)

avoid:A quiet day on auction Sunday.name: A quiet day on auction Sunday
avoid:A quiet day on auction Sunday.teaser: The third weekend of November, Beaune is the loudest it gets all year
avoid:A quiet day on auction Sunday.story: If the plan is a slow walk round the ramparts and an empty cellar, do not pick the Hospices auction weekend, Les Trois Glorieuses. For those days the town fills shoulder to shoulder: the sale under the Halles, light projections on the monuments and queues at every tasting door, hotels booked months out and tables gone weeks before. It is a spectacle worth seeing on purpose. It is not the calm Beaune this guide is written for, and a crew arriving by chance that Sunday will spend the day in a crowd.
avoid:A quiet day on auction Sunday.why: Choose the weekend deliberately, either to be in the crowd or to be anywhere else.
facts: Check the auction dates on the hot board and the calendar before fixing the shore day
Come the week before, when the new wines are in barrel and the streets are empty, or on the Monday after

avoid:Tasting and driving the Route.name: Tasting and driving the Route
avoid:Tasting and driving the Route.teaser: Pommard, Volnay, Meursault, three tastings and a car: France's limit is 0.5 g/l
avoid:Tasting and driving the Route.story: Driving the Route des Grands Crus from one tasting room to the next is the obvious plan and the wrong one. In France the legal limit is 0.5 g of alcohol per litre of blood; for anyone on a probationary licence, the first three years (two after accompanied driving), it is 0.2 g/l, which one glass can pass. From 0.8 g/l it is a criminal offence. Each glass adds roughly 0.2 to 0.25 g/l. The vines are flat enough to walk or cycle, and the TER stops in the wine villages.
avoid:Tasting and driving the Route.why: Name one driver who stays dry, or leave the car in Beaune and let your legs do the Côte.
facts: Count on 0.5 g/l as the ceiling (0.2 g/l on a new licence) and plan the day around it
Walk from Beaune to Meursault through the vines; hire a bike from Bourgogne Evasion (allée du Docteur Bouley) for the signed Voie des Vignes, about 22 km to Santenay; or book a driver

follow:Beaune tourist office.name: Beaune tourist office
follow:Beaune tourist office.teaser: The Office de Tourisme's site sells the bookable side of Beaune: mill visits, workshops, tastings
follow:Beaune tourist office.story: The Office de Tourisme de Beaune et Pays Beaunois runs a French site and an English twin, and behind both sits a booking platform that is more useful than the brochures. That is where the Fallot mill tours, the barrel-making workshop at Vignoles and many cellar tastings are sold by time slot, with the current price shown. Its events pages carry the town's agenda week by week, from the ramparts tours in autumn to the auction weekend. Check it the night before a shore day: listings there change faster than any printed guide.

follow:Hospices de Beaune.name: Hospices de Beaune
follow:Hospices de Beaune.teaser: The Hospices' own site: the Hôtel-Dieu visit, the vineyard estate and the November sale
follow:Hospices de Beaune.story: The Hospices de Beaune publish their own site, and it is where the November sale is announced, with its cuvées listed by name. It also carries the practical side of the Hôtel-Dieu visit and news of the estate's vineyards across the Côte. The proceeds still go to the hospital and the care homes the Hospices run, so every bid at the sale pays for care in the town. Follow it in the weeks before the auction to see which cuvées are on offer.

follow:Bourgogne Wines (BIVB).name: Bourgogne Wines (BIVB)
follow:Bourgogne Wines (BIVB).teaser: The trade body's site: every appellation, the climats, and the courses of the École des Vins
follow:Bourgogne Wines (BIVB).story: The Bureau Interprofessionnel des Vins de Bourgogne, the growers' and merchants' joint body based in Beaune, keeps bourgogne-wines.com as the reference for the region. It has a page for each appellation, from regional Bourgogne to the grands crus, with maps, soils and grape varieties, and an explanation of how the climats fit together. It also runs the École des Vins de Bourgogne, whose tastings and courses are held at the Cité des Climats in Beaune and at the Cité de la Gastronomie in Dijon. Look up a village on it before you taste.

follow:Raisin.name: Raisin

follow:Raisin.story: Raisin is a map and app of bars, restaurants and wine shops that pour natural wine, filled in by the venues and by drinkers who post what they ate and opened. follow:Festival d'Opéra Baroque.name: Festival d'Opéra Baroque et Romantique
follow:Festival d'Opéra Baroque.teaser: The July opera festival's own site: programme, casts and the day tickets open
follow:Festival d'Opéra Baroque.story: Beaune's summer opera festival, founded in 1983 by Anne Blanchard and Kader Hassissi, now goes by Festival International d'Opéra Baroque et Romantique and has had Maximilien Hondermarck as artistic director since 2025. Its site carries each year's programme of operas, oratorios and recitals, built weekend by weekend around a composer or a period, with the venues: the courtyard of the Hospices, the Basilique Notre-Dame and, since 2026, the Théâtre de Beaune. The next programme had not been published when we checked in October 2026; follow the site for the announcement and the opening of ticket sales.

listening:No hi-fi listening bar.name: No hi-fi listening bar
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.teaser: No listening bar in the Japanese jazz-kissa sense, in Beaune or in Dijon, that we could find
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.story: A listening bar, in the sense the term now carries, is a room built around a serious hi-fi system and a wall of vinyl, where people come to hear records played whole rather than to talk over them. We looked for one in Beaune and in Dijon in October 2026 and found none; in France such rooms cluster in Paris, with a few in cities such as Lille. Beaune's equivalent is quieter and older: a cold cellar at dusk, a glass, and someone at the counter who will explain what is in it.
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.why: Swap the turntable for the counter: the conversation over the glass is the town's evening ritual.
facts: An evening glass at a counter where the person pouring knows the grower

listening:The cellar-and-counter night.name: The cellar-and-counter night
listening:The cellar-and-counter night.teaser: A Beaune evening is a glass, a counter and a conversation, centred on Place Madeleine
listening:The cellar-and-counter night.story: Beaune has no club worth the walk, and its evening does not pretend otherwise. The town after dark is the eastern side, Place Madeleine and its faubourg, where Caves Madeleine seats people at shared tables and Le Comptoir des Tontons pours natural wine among the shelves of its épicerie. A few streets away, Enstase opens its kitchen at the end of the week, Thursday and Friday, for bao and small plates beside the natural-wine list. Start with a glass at one, eat at another, and finish with the last pour from someone who can tell you who made it.
listening:The cellar-and-counter night.why: Go on a Thursday or Friday, when the Enstase kitchen is open and the faubourg is at its fullest.
facts: Place Madeleine and the Faubourg Madeleine; Enstase at 5 rue Vergnette de Lamotte

listening:La Vapeur, Dijon.name: La Vapeur, Dijon
listening:La Vapeur, Dijon.teaser: Dijon's contemporary-music hall: concerts most weeks, and the SIRK electronic month every April
listening:La Vapeur, Dijon.story: For a loud night that Beaune cannot give, go north to Dijon. La Vapeur, on avenue de Stalingrad by the Toison d'Or tram stop, is the city's state-labelled contemporary-music venue (SMAC), with a programme of rap, pop, electronic and stage shows. Late in November 2026 its listings include the drag performer Piche on the 21st and the singer Wallace Cleaver on the 26th, presenting his album 'Marcel'. Every April it runs Le SIRK, a month of electronic nights across Dijon venues; the tenth edition, in 2025, brought SHERELLE, Steffi and Luciano.
listening:La Vapeur, Dijon.why: Check the programme before you go: a good night in a mid-sized room for the price of a bottle.
facts: 42 avenue de Stalingrad, Dijon (tram T1, Toison d'Or); about 45 minutes by road from Beaune

craft:Do this one.name: Art du Tonneau, Vignoles
craft:Do this one.teaser: Build a 228-litre Burgundy barrel with your own hands, five minutes from the ramparts
craft:Do this one.story: Every great Burgundy spends its first year in oak, and the Côte still makes its own barrels: at Saint-Romain, on the hill above Meursault, the François family has been coopering since 1910. At Art du Tonneau, a family cooperage on the edge of Vignoles, five minutes from Beaune, you do the work yourself. Frédéric Gillet and his team run the workshop: first the woods and the history of the trade, then, in teams of three to five, you raise the staves, drive the hoops and assemble a 228-litre Burgundy pièce, the barrel of the Côte. A glass of Chardonnay closes the session.
craft:Do this one.why: It is the only time most people will feel how a barrel is held together: by iron, pressure and nothing else.
facts: Hands-on initiation: the history and the woods, then teams of 3 to 5 assemble a 228-litre Burgundy barrel; optional Chardonnay tasting; in French, English or German on request

craft:Other one.name: The Fallot mustard mill
craft:Other one.teaser: Watch Beaune's mustard being made in the Faubourg Bretonnière, then taste it at the mustard bar
craft:Other one.story: The Fallot house still makes mustard in its works on the Faubourg Bretonnière, and it opens the floor to visitors. The 'Sensations Fortes' route takes you through the production workshops, where the seed is ground and the paste mixed, and ends at a mustard bar for tasting; a gentler 'Découvertes' route tells the history. Each lasts about an hour, in French, English or German, by time slot. The smell of crushed seed is the thing you carry home. Missing: you watch the craft, you do not practise it, and no master teaches you.
craft:Other one.why: Take the production route, not the history route: the workshop floor is the point.
facts: A guided walk through the production workshops, ending with a tasting at the mustard bar

craft:What is sold as Burgundy-made.name: What is sold as Burgundy-made
craft:What is sold as Burgundy-made.teaser: 'Moutarde de Dijon' is a recipe, not a place: most of the seed in it is Canadian
craft:What is sold as Burgundy-made.story: The shelves around the Hôtel-Dieu and Place Carnot sell jar after jar of 'moutarde de Dijon', and the name promises less than it seems. It is a method, brown seed ground with an acid, and the term is not legally tied to Dijon or to Burgundy. Canada supplies roughly 80 per cent of the seed used in French mustard, and French growers, almost all in Burgundy, cover only around a fifth, which is why the 2022 Canadian drought emptied French supermarket shelves. The jar that promises Burgundian seed carries the protected name 'Moutarde de Bourgogne' IGP. The snail on the souvenir menu is the plate's own warning.
craft:What is sold as Burgundy-made.why: Turn the jar round: 'IGP Moutarde de Bourgogne' on the label, not 'Dijon' on the front, is the Burgundian one.
facts: Read the back of a mustard jar for 'IGP Moutarde de Bourgogne' and the origin of the seed

_notes: 17 WebSearch calls. Craft pick: Art du Tonneau (cooperage, Vignoles): the only candidate that is truly hands-on with open, bookable sessions and a named person (Frédéric Gillet) running them, in a craft that is unbroken on the Côte (François Frères at Saint-Romain since 1910); his formal title (master cooper?) is not confirmed. Fallot = a watched tour, no class; École des Vins = open enrolment but no named teacher and tasting rather than making. Mulot & Petitjean's Dijon factory museum (about 1 h, tasting) was the fourth candidate: a visit, not a class, no named master; Saint-Romain cooperages (François Frères, Damy, Cadus) show no public visits in results; Cassissium not checked. Gaps: IGP Moutarde de Bourgogne specification (Burgundy seed, Burgundy white wine) not re-read at INAO, so the card says only that the jar promising Burgundian seed carries the IGP; 80% Canada figure is from 2022. Snail import origins from an encyclopedia only (no countries printed). Enstase hours conflict on Raisin; chef name from the old card unsourced and removed. La Vapeur official URL not confirmed (site left empty); 2026 November listings partial. bourgogne-wines.com, hospices-beaune.com and festivalbeaune.com are given as official from knowledge, not each confirmed by a search hit. No listening-bar search for Beaune or Lyon specifically. Art du Tonneau has no confirmed own website (site empty, book via tourist office).
